title: The manager keeps working on more Macs, and knows how Macs like yours are doing

highlights.title: Fixes that kept the manager from running
highlights.detail: Setting up pre-warming no longer loops on "Provider settings changed". Bloomkeeper now accepts the launch settings Darkbloom writes for itself. The manager stays on across app and Darkbloom updates, and when it does turn off it says why. It restarts a provider that Darkbloom left drained, works while Darkbloom preloads at startup, handles a new device key, and turns on with a stopped pair. If Darkbloom is set to serve 3 or more models, Bloomkeeper says so and tells you how to pick one. Also works with Darkbloom 0.9.11.

highlights.title: Macs like yours
highlights.detail: The Pulse shows how this Mac's requests compare with Macs of the same chip and memory on the same model. If they're getting work and this Mac isn't, Bloomkeeper treats it as a stall and recovers sooner.

highlights.title: "It's not you"
highlights.detail: When Darkbloom has a network-wide problem, a banner says so, and Bloomkeeper holds off restarts and automatic problem reports until it's over.

highlights.title: Smarter excursions
highlights.detail: Macs that can hold a larger model try it when public data shows it clearly paying more and its demand is high for the time of day, at most once a week per model until Bloomkeeper has its own pay data for it. A model that pays less than home needs stronger evidence for the next two weeks. New Macs start on the model that pays best on Macs like them, with a notice and a one-tap Keep.

highlights.title: Network news
highlights.detail: The Optimizer tab lists models joining or leaving the network and big changes in how many Macs have them loaded, and flags a model your Mac still offers after the network dropped it.
